model.rationale: A D+32 electorate, a favorable environment for Democrats, and a massive resource gap between Brad Lander and an essentially unfunded Republican opponent make the Democratic hold near-certain; markets price the race at about 98% Democratic.
model.watch: Any late outside spending targeting Lander or polling showing an unexpectedly tight race would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Dan Goldman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
New York's 10th District is among the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+32. Dan Goldman lost renomination, and City Comptroller Brad Lander enters the general election as the Democratic nominee, having raised about $2.7 million. Republican Jennifer Moore has reported raising under $3,000, with no outside spending on either side so far.

With no public general-election polling, the forecast rests on the district's deep-blue electorate, a national environment favoring Democrats, and the stark resource gap. Prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's chances near 98 percent. The seat is rated Safe Democratic; the main uncertainty is the size of the winning margin, not which party prevails.
